core_obligations: Reduce to a comparison of extension groups: since Ab(C) is the category of modules over the constant sheaf Z, apply the Ext^1-H^1 identification twice and observe that it remains to show Ext^1_{Mod(O)}(O, F) = Ext^1_{Mod(Z)}(Z, F_ab) (proof lines 438-449).

One direction: from an extension 0 -> F -> E -> O -> 0 in Mod(O), pull it back along the obvious map of abelian sheaves Z -> O, which produces the extension E_ab displayed as a map of short exact sequences (proof lines 450-468).

The other direction: from an extension 0 -> F_ab -> E_ab -> Z -> 0 in Mod(Z), tensor with O, use flatness of Z over Z to keep the sequence exact, replace Z tensor_Z O by O and push out along the O-linear multiplication map F tensor_Z O -> F, obtaining the desired extension 0 -> F -> E -> O -> 0 (proof lines 469-504); the author omits the verification that the two constructions are mutually inverse (proof lines 505-506).
proof_roadmap: Translate both H^1 groups into Ext^1 groups and reduce to comparing extensions of O by F with extensions of Z by F_ab (proof lines 438-449).
Construct the map from extensions of O to extensions of Z by pullback along Z -> O (proof lines 450-468).
Construct the inverse by tensoring with O and pushing out along the multiplication map, leaving the double-composition check to the reader (proof lines 469-506).
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two cohomology groups computed in different abelian categories: H^1(C, F_ab) for the underlying abelian sheaf and H^1(C, F) for the O-module (statement lines 423-434). The proof reduces the statement to a comparison of extension groups and then has to build the correspondence explicitly: one direction is a pullback along the map Z -> O of abelian sheaves, while the other is genuinely two steps, tensoring an extension of Z by F_ab with O and then pushing out along the O-linear multiplication map F tensor_Z O -> F, the legality of which rests on flatness of Z (proof lines 469-504). The author explicitly leaves the verification that the two constructions are inverse to the reader, and that sentence is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: two explicit constructions, one flatness input.
